source: Aligned to ASQ, IASSC, and ISO 13053 Bodies of Knowledge

belts.name: White Belt
belts.audience: New employees, frontline staff, supervisors, and anyone joining an improvement project for the first time.
belts.prerequisites: None. Start here with zero prior knowledge.
belts.previousRecap: No previous belt. This course starts with the shared language of quality, waste, variation, and DMAIC.
outcomes: Explain what Lean Six Sigma is and where it came from
Recognize waste, variation, defects, and cost of poor quality
Describe VOC, CTQ, DMAIC, and the belt roles
Contribute useful data and ideas to a team project

modules.title: Quality Foundations
modules.summary: Build the shared language of quality: where Six Sigma and Lean came from, why poor quality costs money, how customers define value, and why variation matters.

lessons.title: History of Six Sigma and Lean
lessons.objective: Trace Six Sigma from Motorola and GE, and Lean from the Toyota Production System.

lessons.title: Quality Basics and Cost of Poor Quality
lessons.objective: Define quality, prevention, appraisal, and failure costs, and calculate a simple COPQ example.

lessons.title: Customers: VOC and CTQ
lessons.objective: Turn customer wants into measurable critical-to-quality requirements.

lessons.title: Variation and Defects
lessons.objective: Explain common and special cause variation and define a defect in plain language.

lessons.title: DMAIC Overview
lessons.objective: Describe the five DMAIC phases and the main question each phase answers.

modules.title: People, Waste, and First Projects
modules.summary: Learn to see the eight wastes, understand who does what on a project, and adopt the culture and habits that make improvement stick.

lessons.title: The 8 Wastes
lessons.objective: Identify the eight wastes in healthcare, retail, manufacturing, IT, banking, and education.

lessons.title: Roles and Responsibilities
lessons.objective: Explain the White, Yellow, Green, Black, and Master Black Belt roles and the sponsor role.

lessons.title: Culture and Mindset
lessons.objective: Describe respect for people, data-based decisions, and a no-blame learning culture.

lessons.title: Your First Improvement Project
lessons.objective: Use a simple A3-style story to plan a small, safe improvement.

project.title: Clean Up a Customer Handoff
project.brief: Pick one handoff you own (for example, a patient transfer, order handoff, or support ticket). Map what happens, identify two wastes, measure how long the handoff takes, test one small change, and confirm the result.

exam.format: 25 multiple-choice questions with four options and explanations.

cheatSheet: COPQ = prevention + appraisal + internal failure + external failure costs
VOC = voice of the customer; CTQ = critical to quality, a measurable customer requirement
DMAIC = Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control
8 wastes = transportation, inventory, motion, waiting, overproduction, overprocessing, defects, skills
nextChecklist: I can explain Lean vs Six Sigma in one sentence each.
I can name the DMAIC phases in order.
I can spot at least three wastes in my own work area.
I can explain what VOC and CTQ mean.

belts.name: Yellow Belt
belts.audience: Team members, supervisors, and process owners who support Green and Black Belt projects.
belts.prerequisites: White Belt or equivalent basic quality awareness.
belts.previousRecap: White Belt recap: quality means meeting customer requirements; waste and variation create defects and cost; DMAIC is the improvement path; everyone has a role.
outcomes: Map a process with SIPOC and a process map
Build a basic project charter and data collection sheet
Use Pareto, fishbone, 5 Whys, check sheets, and basic charts
Contribute to brainstorming, 5S, and team-based improvement
Explain how a control plan and a basic control chart sustain an improvement

modules.title: Process Thinking
modules.summary: See work as a process with suppliers, inputs, steps, outputs, and customers. Learn to define process boundaries and draw what actually happens, not what people think happens.

lessons.title: Process Thinking
lessons.objective: Explain inputs, outputs, boundaries, and the customer of a process.

lessons.title: SIPOC
lessons.objective: Build a Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs, Customers diagram.

lessons.title: Process Mapping
lessons.objective: Create a swimlane or flowchart and flag handoffs and decision points.

modules.title: DMAIC, Charters, and Control
modules.summary: Go deeper into DMAIC and learn the basic charter questions: why the project exists, what is in scope, how success is measured, and who is accountable. Finish with the Control phase so the gain is held after the project closes.

lessons.title: DMAIC in Detail
lessons.objective: List the key activities and deliverables of each DMAIC phase.

lessons.title: Project Charter Basics
lessons.objective: Write a problem statement, goal, scope, team, and milestone plan.

lessons.title: Control Plans and Basic SPC
lessons.objective: Build a control plan and read a basic control chart so the improvement is sustained.

modules.title: Data and Basic Charts
modules.summary: Collect trustworthy data and display it honestly. Practice check sheets, run charts, histograms, bar charts, and Pareto analysis.

lessons.title: Data Types
lessons.objective: Distinguish continuous and discrete data and choose a suitable summary.

lessons.title: Check Sheets
lessons.objective: Design a simple form that makes data easy to record and verify.

lessons.title: Basic Charts
lessons.objective: Choose and interpret run charts, histograms, and bar charts.

lessons.title: Pareto Analysis
lessons.objective: Use the 80/20 rule to prioritize the few causes that create most of the problem.

modules.title: Root Cause and Lean Basics
modules.summary: Move from symptoms to causes using fishbone and 5 Whys, then remove everyday friction with 5S and basic Lean thinking.

lessons.title: Fishbone Diagram
lessons.objective: Brainstorm causes across people, process, equipment, materials, measurement, and environment.

lessons.title: 5 Whys
lessons.objective: Ask focused why questions until the actionable root cause is found.

lessons.title: 5S
lessons.objective: Apply sort, set in order, shine, standardize, and sustain.

lessons.title: Basic Lean
lessons.objective: Use value, flow, pull, and perfection to reduce waiting and rework.

modules.title: People and Teamwork
modules.summary: Generate better ideas and help a team make decisions without losing the quiet voices or the evidence.

lessons.title: Brainstorming
lessons.objective: Run silent idea generation and affinity grouping before judging ideas.

lessons.title: Teamwork
lessons.objective: Define roles, ground rules, decision rules, and meeting habits for an improvement team.

project.title: Reduce Waiting in a Service Process
project.brief: Map one service process with SIPOC and a flowchart, collect two weeks of waiting-time data on a check sheet, build a Pareto chart of delay reasons, run a 5 Whys on the top reason, and draft a one-page control plan for the improved process.

exam.format: 40 multiple-choice questions with four options and explanations.

cheatSheet: SIPOC = Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs, Customers
Pareto principle: roughly 80% of effects come from about 20% of causes
5 Whys: ask why until you reach a cause you can act on
5S = Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain
Control plan = metric, target, monitoring method, frequency, owner, and reaction plan
nextChecklist: I can draw a SIPOC for a process I own.
I can build a check sheet and a Pareto chart.
I can facilitate a 5 Whys without blaming a person.
I can explain how 5S supports flow.
I can draft a control plan and read a basic control chart.

belts.name: Green Belt
belts.audience: Project leaders and process owners who run DMAIC projects part-time with a Black Belt or sponsor.
belts.prerequisites: Yellow Belt or equivalent process improvement experience.
belts.previousRecap: Yellow Belt recap: processes have suppliers, inputs, steps, outputs, and customers; data must be collected consistently; Pareto, fishbone, and 5 Whys help find causes.
outcomes: Lead a small-to-medium DMAIC project from charter to control
Plan data collection, sampling, and measurement system studies
Use descriptive statistics, capability, hypothesis tests, and simple regression
Select and pilot solutions and hand off a control plan

modules.title: Define
modules.summary: Turn a vague complaint into a bounded project with a clear customer, measurable goal, and named stakeholders.

lessons.title: Project Charter
lessons.objective: Write a problem statement, goal, scope, business case, team, and timeline.

lessons.title: Stakeholders
lessons.objective: Map influence and interest and plan engagement.

lessons.title: VOC and CTQ
lessons.objective: Translate customer language into measurable CTQs and specifications.

modules.title: Measure
modules.summary: Build a trustworthy measurement system, describe the data, and compare process performance with customer specifications.

lessons.title: Data Collection Plan
lessons.objective: Define what, where, when, who, and how to collect data.

lessons.title: Sampling
lessons.objective: Choose random, stratified, or systematic samples and avoid bias.

lessons.title: Measurement System Analysis
lessons.objective: Run a Gage R&R and interpret %GRR and number of distinct categories.

lessons.title: Descriptive Statistics
lessons.objective: Calculate and interpret mean, median, standard deviation, and range.

lessons.title: Normal Distribution
lessons.objective: Use the 68-95-99.7 rule and check normality before capability analysis.

lessons.title: Sigma Level and DPMO
lessons.objective: Convert defects and opportunities into DPMO and sigma level.

lessons.title: Cp and Cpk
lessons.objective: Calculate capability indices and explain the difference between potential and actual capability.

modules.title: Analyze
modules.summary: Use graphs, root cause tools, risk analysis, and statistical tests to separate real causes from noise.

lessons.title: Graphs and Data Displays
lessons.objective: Select histograms, box plots, run charts, and scatter plots for the question.

lessons.title: Root Cause Analysis
lessons.objective: Combine fishbone, 5 Whys, stratification, and process observation.

lessons.title: FMEA
lessons.objective: Score severity, occurrence, and detection and prioritize failure modes.

lessons.title: Hypothesis Testing Basics
lessons.objective: Form null and alternative hypotheses and interpret p-values correctly.

lessons.title: Correlation
lessons.objective: Measure the strength and direction of a linear relationship.

lessons.title: Simple Regression
lessons.objective: Fit a line, interpret slope and R-squared, and check residuals.

lessons.title: ANOVA Introduction
lessons.objective: Compare means across three or more groups and read the F-test.

modules.title: Improve
modules.summary: Choose solutions with evidence, test them safely, mistake-proof the process, and begin designing experiments.

lessons.title: Solution Selection
lessons.objective: Use impact, effort, risk, and cost to choose among candidate solutions.

lessons.title: Pilot Testing
lessons.objective: Design a small trial with clear success measures and a rollback plan.

lessons.title: Poka-Yoke
lessons.objective: Add mistake-proofing devices or checks that prevent or detect errors.

lessons.title: Lean Tools for Improvement
lessons.objective: Apply flow, pull, standard work, and quick changeover thinking.

lessons.title: DOE Introduction
lessons.objective: Explain factors, levels, responses, and why experiments beat one-factor tests.

modules.title: Control
modules.summary: Keep the gains by monitoring the process, documenting the new standard, and assigning clear ownership.

lessons.title: Control Charts
lessons.objective: Select X-bar/R, I-MR, p, np, c, or u charts and apply basic rules.

lessons.title: Control Plans
lessons.objective: Document metrics, sampling, reactions, and owners.

lessons.title: SOPs and Standardization
lessons.objective: Write usable standard work and train to it.

modules.title: Project Management and Software
modules.summary: Run the project professionally and use Excel or Minitab for the core analyses.

lessons.title: Project Management
lessons.objective: Plan tasks, manage risks, communicate status, and close the project.

lessons.title: Excel and Minitab Basics
lessons.objective: Use descriptive statistics, control charts, capability, and t-tests in software.

project.title: Reduce Appointment No-Shows
project.brief: Charter a project to reduce no-shows in a clinic, bank branch, or service center. Build a data plan, check the measurement system, baseline the no-show rate, run a Pareto and hypothesis test, pilot a reminder solution, and hand off a control chart and control plan.

exam.format: 60 multiple-choice questions with four options and explanations, including calculations.

cheatSheet: Z = (X - mean) / standard deviation
DPMO = defects / (units x opportunities) x 1,000,000
Cp = (USL - LSL) / 6 sigma; Cpk = min((USL - mean)/3 sigma, (mean - LSL)/3 sigma)
p-value < alpha: reject the null hypothesis
nextChecklist: I can build a data collection plan and a sampling plan.
I can interpret a Gage R&R and a capability report.
I can choose a basic hypothesis test for a question.
I can hand off a control chart and control plan.

belts.name: Black Belt
belts.audience: Full-time improvement leaders who lead complex, cross-functional projects and coach Green Belts.
belts.prerequisites: Green Belt certification and completion of at least one DMAIC project.
belts.previousRecap: Green Belt recap: DMAIC projects need a charter, trustworthy measurement, capability analysis, hypothesis tests, pilots, and control plans; simple regression and ANOVA support decisions.
outcomes: Lead complex DMAIC and design projects across functions
Apply advanced statistics, regression, and designed experiments
Handle attribute measurement systems, non-normal data, and advanced SPC
Integrate Lean, DFSS, change leadership, finance, and mentoring

modules.title: Probability and Inference
modules.summary: Build the statistical foundation for advanced decision-making: distributions, sampling, confidence, power, and the full hypothesis testing toolkit.

lessons.title: Probability Distributions
lessons.objective: Recognize normal, binomial, Poisson, exponential, and Weibull patterns.

lessons.title: Sampling Distributions and the Central Limit Theorem
lessons.objective: Explain why sample means behave predictably.

lessons.title: Confidence Intervals
lessons.objective: Interpret interval estimates for means, proportions, and differences.

lessons.title: Power and Sample Size
lessons.objective: Balance alpha, beta, effect size, and sample size.

lessons.title: Choosing the Right Hypothesis Test
lessons.objective: Select a test from the data type, number of groups, and assumptions.

lessons.title: t-Tests
lessons.objective: Run one-sample, two-sample, and paired t-tests.

lessons.title: ANOVA
lessons.objective: Run one-way and two-way ANOVA and interpret interactions.

lessons.title: Non-Parametric Tests
lessons.objective: Use Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis, and sign tests when assumptions fail.

lessons.title: Chi-Square Tests
lessons.objective: Test independence and goodness of fit for categorical data.

modules.title: Measurement Systems
modules.summary: Extend MSA to pass/fail and categorical judgments, and understand calibration and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Attribute MSA
lessons.objective: Run attribute agreement analysis and interpret kappa.

lessons.title: Measurement Uncertainty and Calibration
lessons.objective: Separate calibration, bias, linearity, and uncertainty.

modules.title: Regression and Modeling
modules.summary: Model relationships with multiple predictors and binary outcomes, then check whether the model is trustworthy.

lessons.title: Multiple Regression
lessons.objective: Interpret coefficients, adjusted R-squared, and overall model tests.

lessons.title: Logistic Regression
lessons.objective: Model yes/no outcomes with odds ratios.

lessons.title: Regression Diagnostics
lessons.objective: Check residuals, leverage, influence, and lack of fit.

lessons.title: Multicollinearity and Model Building
lessons.objective: Detect correlated predictors and choose a parsimonious model.

modules.title: Design of Experiments
modules.summary: Design efficient experiments, screen many factors, optimize responses, and make designs robust to noise.

lessons.title: Full Factorial DOE
lessons.objective: Design and analyze a full factorial with main effects and interactions.

lessons.title: Fractional Factorial DOE
lessons.objective: Screen many factors with resolution III, IV, and V designs.

lessons.title: Blocking and Randomization
lessons.objective: Protect experiments from nuisance variables.

lessons.title: Response Surface Methods
lessons.objective: Find optimum settings with central composite or Box-Behnken designs.

lessons.title: Robust Design and Taguchi
lessons.objective: Reduce sensitivity to noise using control and noise factors.

modules.title: Advanced SPC and Capability
modules.summary: Monitor complex processes with advanced charts and handle capability when data are not normal or runs are short.

lessons.title: Advanced SPC
lessons.objective: Use CUSUM, EWMA, and multivariate charts appropriately.

lessons.title: Non-Normal Capability
lessons.objective: Transform data or fit a distribution before calculating capability.

lessons.title: Short-Run SPC
lessons.objective: Monitor small batches with standardized or target charts.

modules.title: Lean and DFSS
modules.summary: Integrate Lean flow tools with Six Sigma and design new processes right the first time with DMADV, QFD, and Kano.

lessons.title: Lean Six Sigma Integration
lessons.objective: Combine waste reduction and variation reduction in one strategy.

lessons.title: Value Stream Mapping
lessons.objective: Map material and information flow and calculate lead time.

lessons.title: TPM
lessons.objective: Improve equipment reliability with autonomous and planned maintenance.

lessons.title: SMED
lessons.objective: Reduce changeover time by separating internal and external work.

lessons.title: Standard Work
lessons.objective: Document the current best method with takt, sequence, and inventory.

lessons.title: 5S and Visual Management
lessons.objective: Create a self-explaining, self-cleaning workplace.

lessons.title: Design for Six Sigma (DMADV)
lessons.objective: Define, Measure, Analyze, Design, and Verify a new process or product.

lessons.title: QFD
lessons.objective: Translate customer needs into design requirements with the House of Quality.

lessons.title: Kano Model
lessons.objective: Classify features as basic, performance, or delighter.

modules.title: Leadership and Finance
modules.summary: Lead complex change, build project pipelines, prove financial benefit, and develop other belts.

lessons.title: Advanced FMEA
lessons.objective: Use action priority, risk review, and integration with control plans.

lessons.title: Change Management
lessons.objective: Use a structured approach to build awareness, desire, knowledge, ability, and reinforcement.

lessons.title: Team Leadership
lessons.objective: Lead cross-functional teams, manage conflict, and make decisions.

lessons.title: Project Selection
lessons.objective: Prioritize projects by impact, feasibility, risk, and strategic fit.

lessons.title: Financial Analysis (COPQ, ROI)
lessons.objective: Build a benefit case with hard and soft savings.

lessons.title: Mentoring
lessons.objective: Coach Green Belts and review project logic and statistics.

project.title: Reduce Turnaround Time and Defects in a Cross-Functional Process
project.brief: Lead a full DMAIC project on a complex process such as loan approvals, patient discharge, or software release. Include MSA, capability, hypothesis testing, regression, a designed experiment, a pilot, and a control plan with financial validation.

exam.format: 100 multiple-choice questions with four options and explanations, including calculations and output interpretation.

cheatSheet: Use non-parametric tests when normality or equal-variance assumptions fail.
R-squared explains variance; adjusted R-squared penalizes extra predictors.
Resolution IV designs do not alias main effects with two-factor interactions.
Capability on non-normal data: transform, fit a distribution, or use non-parametric methods.
nextChecklist: I can choose and interpret a hypothesis test from a scenario.
I can build and diagnose a multiple regression model.
I can design and analyze a screening experiment.
I can lead a cross-functional project and mentor a Green Belt.

belts.name: Master Black Belt
belts.audience: Experienced Black Belts who design deployments, govern portfolios, consult on statistics, and build organizational capability.
belts.prerequisites: Black Belt certification and a track record of leading complex projects.
belts.previousRecap: Black Belt recap: complex projects need advanced statistics, designed experiments, Lean and DFSS, change leadership, and validated financial benefits.
outcomes: Deploy strategy with Hoshin Kanri and govern an improvement portfolio
Validate financial benefits and select projects by strategic value
Coach Black Belts and consult on advanced statistical questions
Design training, build culture, and integrate analytics and Industry 4.0
Apply ISO 13053, ASQ, and IASSC certification standards and ethics

modules.title: Strategy Deployment
modules.summary: Connect improvement work to strategy through Hoshin Kanri, governance, portfolio selection, and validated financial benefits.

lessons.title: Hoshin Kanri
lessons.objective: Cascade strategic objectives into annual improvement priorities.

lessons.title: Strategy Deployment and Catchball
lessons.objective: Use catchball to align goals, resources, and measures.

lessons.title: Program Governance
lessons.objective: Design steering committees, review cadence, and escalation paths.

lessons.title: Project Portfolio Selection
lessons.objective: Balance impact, risk, capacity, and strategic fit.

lessons.title: Financial Validation
lessons.objective: Verify hard savings, avoid double counting, and track realization.

modules.title: Coaching and Consulting
modules.summary: Develop belts and leaders through coaching, mentoring, statistical consulting, and training design.

lessons.title: Coaching Belts
lessons.objective: Use questions, observation, and feedback to improve project thinking.

lessons.title: Mentoring and Capability Building
lessons.objective: Build a pipeline of belts and subject-matter experts.

lessons.title: Statistical Consulting
lessons.objective: Diagnose analysis problems and recommend defensible methods.

lessons.title: Training Design
lessons.objective: Design practice-based curricula with assessment and transfer.

modules.title: Enterprise Transformation
modules.summary: Scale improvement across the enterprise with DFSS, change management, culture, balanced scorecards, and benchmarking.

lessons.title: Enterprise DFSS
lessons.objective: Deploy design methods across product, service, and process development.

lessons.title: Organizational Change
lessons.objective: Use change models, stakeholder plans, and reinforcement.

lessons.title: Culture Building
lessons.objective: Make improvement, respect, and data-based decisions part of daily work.

lessons.title: Balanced Scorecard
lessons.objective: Connect financial, customer, process, and learning measures.

lessons.title: Benchmarking
lessons.objective: Compare performance with best-in-class processes and adapt practices.

modules.title: Analytics and Industry 4.0
modules.summary: Integrate modern analytics, automation, and data governance into improvement work.

lessons.title: Analytics and Industry 4.0
lessons.objective: Use sensors, dashboards, predictive models, and automation.

lessons.title: Data Governance and Ethics
lessons.objective: Protect privacy, ensure data quality, and use analytics responsibly.

modules.title: Standards and Certification
modules.summary: Understand the standards and ethical expectations behind certification and deployment.

lessons.title: ISO 13053
lessons.objective: Explain the ISO standard for Six Sigma methods and roles.

lessons.title: ASQ and IASSC Standards
lessons.objective: Compare certification bodies, BoKs, and exam expectations.

lessons.title: Certification and Ethics
lessons.objective: Apply truthfulness, competence, confidentiality, and conflict-of-interest rules.

modules.title: Leadership and Value
modules.summary: Lead a deployment, prove value, and sustain improvement beyond individual projects.

lessons.title: Change Leadership
lessons.objective: Lead leaders through resistance, politics, and competing priorities.

lessons.title: ROI and Benefits Realization
lessons.objective: Track costs, benefits, cash flow, and value over time.

lessons.title: Capstone: Leading a Deployment
lessons.objective: Build a deployment roadmap, governance model, and measurement plan.

project.title: Build an Enterprise Improvement Deployment Plan
project.brief: Create a 12-month deployment plan for a multi-site organization: strategy map, Hoshin priorities, governance, portfolio, training pipeline, financial validation, and a balanced scorecard.

exam.format: 100 case-based multiple-choice questions with four options and explanations.

cheatSheet: Hoshin Kanri aligns breakthrough objectives with daily management.
Hard savings affect the P&L or cash flow; soft savings are avoided or theoretical costs.
Portfolio selection balances value, risk, capacity, and strategic fit.
ISO 13053 describes Six Sigma methods and roles; ASQ and IASSC define BoKs and exams.
nextChecklist: I can link a project portfolio to strategic objectives.
I can coach a Black Belt through a statistical disagreement.
I can design a training and certification pathway.
I can validate financial benefits without double counting.
